original_question: For which separable Banach spaces X are the Hilbertian sum ℓ_2(X) and the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_2([0, 1], X) isomorphic as Banach spaces?
target_in_paper: Problem 5.5 (Diestel) in §5.2, Structural properties: determine for which separable Banach spaces X the spaces ℓ_2(X) and L_2([0,1],X) are isomorphic. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact problem targeted in the paper, uses the correct two Banach-space constructions, keeps the crucial separability hypothesis on X, and asks the right isomorphic-classification question rather than the neighboring unconditional-basis problem (Problem 5.4) or the containment problem (Problem 5.6). ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works throughout with real Banach spaces. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
The interval [0,1] is understood to be equipped with Lebesgue measure λ. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))

L_2([0,1],X) is meant in the Lebesgue-Bochner sense: equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X such that ∫_0^1 ||f(t)||^2 dλ(t) < ∞, with the usual Bochner L_2 norm. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
ℓ_2(X) should be read as the countable ℓ_2-direct sum of copies of X, i.e. sequences (x_n) in X with Σ_n ||x_n||^2 < ∞, with the usual ℓ_2 norm.

The intended notion of 'isomorphic' is Banach-space isomorphism, i.e. linear isomorphism with bounded inverse; your draft suggests this by saying 'as Banach spaces,' but the paper states it more tersely. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a separable real Banach space. For which such X is the countable Hilbertian direct sum ℓ_2(X) = { (x_n) : x_n ∈ X, Σ_{n=1}^∞ ||x_n||^2 < ∞ } linearly isomorphic, as a Banach space, to the Lebesgue-Bochner space L_2([0,1],X) of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f:[0,1]→X with ∫_0^1 ||f(t)||^2 dλ(t) < ∞, where λ is Lebesgue measure on [0,1]?
justification: This is exactly Problem 5.5 in §5.2. The immediately preceding context shows the intended scope and sharpness: the paper notes that ℓ_2 and L_2[0,1] are isomorphic, but that ℓ_2(X) and L_2([0,1],X) are not isomorphic in general, giving X = c_0 as an example. The standing notation and the opening of §5 supply the hidden assumptions needed to make the question fully stand-alone: all Banach spaces are real, [0,1] carries Lebesgue measure λ, and L_p(μ,X) denotes the usual Lebesgue-Bochner space of strongly measurable p-integrable X-valued functions. ([webs.um.es](https://webs.um.es/joserr/miwiki/lib/exe/fetch.php?cache=cache&id=papers&media=openproblems.pdf))
